s: The car screen project tested the unit and found it runs older software than advertised, so a return and a better replacement joined the Board; a radio-style home screen mockup went up to try on it.

A new desktop tool can pin any window on top, see-through, for framing shots; the site menu got a tighter grid with drifting clouds and slowly panning photos; the car screen project got a build plan and a local test page.

The footage machine now listens to each clip's sound and checks sharpness; a first desktop app for it shipped with two quick fixes; the site got a carspotting billboard gallery, a bubbly channel-style menu and new inspiration lines; two new plans joined the Board.

The footage machine now reads iPhone photos anywhere, stops flagging screenshots as duplicates and ran its first real sort; a first video editor landed that auto-cuts dead air and filler words; the head unit launcher got a radio-style look.

Built the footage machine's first sorter (it now reads iPhone HEIC photos), moved 12.9 GB of phone footage onto the SSD, scaffolded automated BeamNG crash test videos, read the Saab head unit's specs, and drew the first bubble launcher for its 7-inch screen.
